advances: Replaces the whole-child-block absolute-variation hypothesis in the bounded adaptive census by a global squared-coefficient budget and a small cubic entropy in every queried block. It controls the complete stopped forward-prefix and local two-inverse-path experiment, including both inverse labels obtained from one shared split block. For each fixed level and continuation length, the successful-row squared-score numerator is bounded by an absolute multiple of its cubic energy. This is a conditional weak-region lemma: it does not select a weak region or prove that a path avoids a remaining strong block.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The canonical tree, chain counts, central-binomial estimate, and source injectivity are from 032423921efad6c8. The scalar function R_3 and its normalization are from 8c94d81c2530b6b1. The local triple coordinate table and its membership and disjointness are from abbc24783c13e0f6. The mixed-row conventions, row sizes, and fixed level-height role are those of 1af079babe686d6e. All fourth-moment, adaptive exponential, stopping, and original-weight estimates are proved above.
proof:
By 032423921efad6c8, there are exactly \(2^m\delta\) chains and \(0<\delta<(Q+1)^{-2}<Q^{-2}\). A chain adds any specified coordinate at most once. Therefore the following three sets of Boolean patterns each have cardinality at most \(2^m\delta\): patterns whose forward successor has a specified label; patterns whose first inverse predecessor has a specified label; and patterns having two predecessors whose second inverse label is specified. For the third assertion, the second inverse label specifies one edge of the chain, and the queried pattern must be the vertex immediately after that edge's upper vertex. There is at most one such vertex for the unique edge with that label in a chain. Requiring two predecessors only makes the set smaller. Also the forward-failure and one-inverse-failure sets each contain one word per chain, and the two-predecessor-failure set contains at most two words per chain. All these sets have fair-block probability at most \(2\delta\). These are separate counts for the two split labels of (2); no independence between them is asserted.

We transfer these counts to the two tilted block laws using a fourth moment. For one bit of parameter \(t\), its density relative to a fair bit is \(f_t(b)=2e^{tb}/(1+e^t)\). Directly,
$$
\mathbb E_{\mathrm{fair}}f_t^4
=R_4(t):=\frac{8(1+e^{4t})}{(1+e^t)^4}
=\frac{\cosh(2t)}{\cosh(t/2)^4}.
\tag{8}
$$
The function \(\log R_4\) is even and vanishes at zero. For \(t\ge0\),
\((\log R_4)'(t)=2(\tanh(2t)-\tanh(t/2))\le3t\), because the derivative of \(\tanh\) is at most one. Integrating proves \(\log R_4(t)\le3t^2/2\le7t^2/4\) for every real \(t\).

For \(0\le x\le1\), \(e^x-1\ge x\) and \(e^x+1\le e+1<4\), so \(\tanh(x/2)\ge x/4\). The formula for \(R_3\) from 8c94d81c2530b6b1 and \(R_3(x)\le4\) give
\(\log R_3(x)\ge(R_3(x)-1)/R_3(x)\ge3x^2/64\). Evenness gives this inequality also for \(-1\le x\le0\). Consequently, for \(a\in\lbrace1,3\rbrace\) and \(|x|\le1\),
\(\log R_4(ax)\le(7/4)a^2x^2\le336\log R_3(x)\).

Consider any available queried block and any of the pattern sets counted above. Let \(E\) denote that set and \(f\) the product density of its \(\mu_{a\lambda}\) law relative to its fair law. Independence inside this fresh block, (1), and (8) show \(\mathbb E_{\mathrm{fair}}f^4\le Q^{336/10000}\). Hölder therefore proves
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu_{a\lambda}(E)
&\le\mathbb P_{\mathrm{fair}}(E)^{3/4}
       (\mathbb E_{\mathrm{fair}}f^4)^{1/4}\\
&\le(2\delta)^{3/4}Q^{84/10000}
\le2Q^{-7/5}=: \rho.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
$$
Indeed \(-3/2+84/10000<-7/5\) and \(2^{3/4}<2\). This bound holds for failure sets and separately for each prescribed forward, first-inverse, or second-inverse label. At an adaptive query, the queried location is known before its bits are exposed. Because this block has not been exposed before, its conditional law is its original independent product block law. Thus (9) is a bound conditional on the entire preceding reveal history, without conditioning on any later success.

We check freshness carefully. The forward prefix exposes child blocks at depths \(s_0,\ldots,s-1\). Its endpoint child block, at depth \(s\), is unexposed. Both inverse labels at that split are functions of this single newly exposed block. The two resulting children differ, so their descendant subtrees are disjoint. Continuation on either branch moves to strictly increasing depths and exposes only child blocks below that branch. Hence no continuation block is a forward block, the split block, or a block in the other branch. Stopping early cannot create a repeated exposure. This proves both distinctness and the query counts in the statement. The subtree coordinates of \(j=z_s(b)\) below its endpoint are exactly those of the original Boolean source, so the block laws used here are indeed laws of the untouched bits, not laws of independently resampled or predecessor-modified blocks.

Pad the reveal sequence by dummy zero exposures to a deterministic horizon of \(2Q\). Before exposure \(\ell\), let \(A_\ell\) be the sum of \(\lambda_u^2\) in its requested block, or zero for a dummy exposure. It is determined by the preceding history. Let \(X_\ell\) be the added contribution to \(S\), with value zero on a failed requirement. An ordinary successful forward or continuation query accepts one label, while a successful split query accepts two labels; hence \(0\le X_\ell\le2\). If \(p_i\) are the conditional probabilities of one accepted label taking its possible values, then \(p_i\le\rho\) by (9) and \(\sum_i p_i\le1\). Cauchy-Schwarz gives
\(\sum_i p_i|\lambda_{vi}|\le(\sum_i p_i\lambda_{vi}^2)^{1/2}\le\sqrt{\rho A_\ell}\). Apply this separately to the two labels at the split. Thus, for every exposure,
$$
\mathbb E[X_\ell\mid\text{preceding history}]
\le2\sqrt{\rho A_\ell},\qquad
\sum_{\ell=1}^{2Q} A_\ell\le100\log Q
\quad\text{on every outcome}.
\tag{10}
$$
The last inequality counts the split block once and follows from distinctness of all exposed blocks and the global budget in (1).

For \(c\ge0\) and \(0\le x\le2\), \(e^{cx}-1\le ce^{2c}x\). Hence (10) gives the conditional exponential bound
\(\mathbb E[e^{cX_\ell}\mid\text{preceding history}]\le\exp(2ce^{2c}\sqrt{\rho A_\ell})\).
It follows by finite conditional expectation that the nonnegative compensated process
$$
\exp\left(c\sum_{\ell=1}^{h}X_\ell
       -2ce^{2c}\sqrt\rho\sum_{\ell=1}^{h}\sqrt{A_\ell}\right),
\qquad 0\le h\le2Q,
\tag{11}
$$
has expectation at most one at every time. No assertion of independence of the increments is used. Pathwise Cauchy-Schwarz in (10) gives \(\sum_{\ell=1}^{2Q}\sqrt{A_\ell}\le\sqrt{200Q\log Q}\). Multiplying (11) at its deterministic terminal time by the resulting deterministic upper bound for its compensator yields
$$
\mathbb E e^{cS}
\le\exp\left(40ce^{2c}Q^{-1/5}\sqrt{\log Q}\right).
\tag{12}
$$
For \(0\le c\le24\), write \(x=\log Q\ge10000\log2\ge5000\). The function \(\sqrt{x}e^{-x/5}\) decreases for \(x\ge5000\), so the exponent in (12) is at most \(96000e^{-952}<1/1000\). The last strict inequality follows, for example, from \(e>2\) and \(2^{27}>96{,}000{,}000\). This proves the exponential assertion of (3).

Every genuine attempted query has conditional failure probability at most \(\rho\), including the single split query. A sequential union bound over the padded horizon gives \(\mathbb P(G^c)\le2Q\rho=4Q^{-2/5}<1/1000\) at the stated threshold. This applies also when \(r=0\), when the only possible failures are forward failures. It proves the remaining assertion of (3).

For the first estimate of (4), \(e^{2U}\mathbf1_{\mathcal P}\le e^{2S}\). For the second, the elementary inequality \(|e^{6U}-1|\le e^{6S}-1\), valid whenever \(|U|\le S\), gives
\(\mathbb E[e^{6U}\mathbf1_G]\ge1-\mathbb P(G^c)-(\mathbb E e^{6S}-1)\).
For \(0<x<1\), the exponential series gives \(e^x\le1/(1-x)\). Thus \(e^{1/1000}<1.002\); the preceding lower bound is greater than \(0.997\), and the original-mass upper bound is less than \(1.002\). These imply (4) with the asserted constants.

On \(G\), the local construction of abbc24783c13e0f6 applies to exactly the two labels and inverse paths just exposed. Its coordinate table changes only \(U_1,\ldots,U_r,V_1,\ldots,V_r\), each by at most one in absolute value, and leaves the entire existing prefix unchanged. The initial two labels are included in \(S\) from the one split query, and every later path coordinate is included at its continuation query. All these coordinates are weak by hypothesis. Therefore every row source satisfies \(|Y_j(x)|\le S\), whence \(V_j\le S^2\). Its triples are pairwise disjoint, avoid \(j\), and have average \(j\), by that accepted construction; it gives precisely \(c_r\) sources after adding the singleton. If \(r=0\), the row contains only \(j\), so its score is zero and no split query is needed.

For \(S\ge0\), \(S^2\le e^{2S}\). Consequently \(e^{6U}V_j\mathbf1_G\le S^2e^{6S}\le e^{8S}\). Equation (3) with \(c=8\) proves (6), including the case \(r=0\).

Finally, (7) is an exact conversion from product expectations to original finite sums. Reduction modulo two recovers the full Boolean source of a level-\(s\) point by 032423921efad6c8. For the fixed data, every source assignment in \(\mathcal P\) gives exactly one such center, and every such center gives exactly one source assignment. Unqueried weak bits remain unrestricted. Normalizing their exponential Boolean weights gives exactly \(P_a\mu_{a\lambda}\), so the three sums in (7), before bounding, are respectively
\(\mathfrak a P_1\mathbb E_{\mu_\lambda}[e^{2U}\mathbf1_{\mathcal P}]\),
\(c_r^2\mathfrak a^3P_3\mathbb E_{\mu_{3\lambda}}[e^{6U}\mathbf1_G]\), and
\(c_r^2\mathfrak a^3P_3\mathbb E_{\mu_{3\lambda}}[e^{6U}V_j\mathbf1_G]\).
Equations (4) and (6) now prove (7).

For completeness, these are the row-score and energy objects of 1af079babe686d6e under the same affine normalization. On each triple the product of its three affine weights equals \(w_j^3\), because its arithmetic mean is \(j\); the singleton has weight \(w_j\). After division by any full original normalizer \(Z\), every cycle's geometric weight is therefore \(p_j=w_j/Z\). Hence the row weights within \(R_j\) are uniform, the row's energy is \(c_r^2w_j^3/Z^3\), and its score variance is exactly (5). The arbitrary fixed-coordinate and common-height contributions cancel in \(Y_j\). The common factor \(c_r^2\mathfrak a^3P_3/Z^3\) cancels between the last two lines of (7); no conditioning on a successful transcript, its split labels, or its inverse paths occurs. On failure the chosen singleton has zero variance. Summing the nonnegative energies over disjoint classes proves the stated mixture conclusion.
statement:
Use the rooted tree, Boolean-source parametrization, and symmetric saturated-chain successor of 032423921efad6c8. Let \(Q\ge2^{10000}\) be an integer, \(m=2(Q+1)^4\), \(\mathcal T_{m,Q}=\bigcup_{h=1}^Q[m]^h\), and \(\delta=2^{-m}\binom m{m/2}\). A node \(v\) of depth less than \(Q\) has child block \(\lbrace vi:i\in[m]\rbrace\), and \(F_m(c)=c+e_{i_m(c)}\) is the successor on the nonterminal set \(D_m\). Any symmetric saturated-chain partition is allowed.

Let \(\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal T_{m,Q}\) be a union of whole, unrevealed child blocks. All coordinates outside \(\mathcal W\) have already been fixed. Let \(\lambda\) denote the real field on \(\mathcal W\), with value zero elsewhere, and suppose
$$
|\lambda_u|\le1\quad(u\in\mathcal W),\qquad
\sum_{u\in\mathcal W}\lambda_u^2\le100\log Q,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^m\log R_3(\lambda_{vi})\le\frac{\log Q}{10000}
\quad\text{for every block that can be queried},
\tag{1}
$$
where \(R_3(x)=4(1+e^{3x})/(1+e^x)^3=1+3\tanh(x/2)^2\) is exactly the scalar function of 8c94d81c2530b6b1. All logarithms are natural. For \(a\in\lbrace1,3\rbrace\), let \(\mu_{a\lambda}\) be the independent Boolean product law on \(\mathcal W\), with \(\mathbb P(b_u=1)=e^{a\lambda_u}/(1+e^{a\lambda_u})\). The fixed data are such that these remaining bits have this law before the experiment begins.

Fix a valid, already determined initial source prefix of length \(s_0\), ending at \(v_0\), where \(v_0=\varnothing\) if \(s_0=0\). Its determining blocks and selected coordinates are part of the fixed data. Fix integers \(s,r\) with \(s_0\le s\le Q\) and \(0\le r\le Q-s\). Apply the following experiment. Every block requested in this experiment, under every possible preceding history, is required to be an unrevealed block in \(\mathcal W\). In particular the experiment never requests a fixed strong block. This is a hypothesis on the chosen experiment, rather than an additional random success condition.

Starting at \(v_0\), attempt exactly \(s-s_0\) forward steps. At each step expose the current child block \(b[v]\). If it is outside \(D_m\), stop the entire experiment in failure; otherwise select \(v i_m(b[v])\) and continue. Let \(\mathcal P\) be the event that all these steps succeed. There is no requirement that the source stop immediately after step \(s\). Let \(U\) be the signed sum of the coefficients at the successfully selected new forward coordinates, stopped on failure, and set \(U=0\) if there are no new forward steps.

If \(\mathcal P\) occurs, its resulting level-\(s\) center is \(j=z_s(b)\), with the fixed prefix included. If \(r=0\), stop successfully and set \(G=\mathcal P\); its row is the singleton \(\lbrace j\rbrace\). If \(r\ge1\), expose the child block of the endpoint \(v\) at depth \(s\). It equals \(j[v]=b[v]\). Require two successive predecessors in its chain, with distinct labels \(i_V,i_U\) satisfying
$$
F_m(j[v]-e_{i_V})=j[v],\qquad
F_m(j[v]-e_{i_V}-e_{i_U})=j[v]-e_{i_V}.
\tag{2}
$$
If either predecessor is absent, stop in failure, accepting neither label. Otherwise accept both labels, put \(U_1=vi_U\) and \(V_1=vi_V\), and attempt the \(r-1\) further inverse steps on the \(U\)-path and then the \(r-1\) further inverse steps on the \(V\)-path. Each inverse step exposes the current node's child block of \(j\), requires that block to belong to \(\operatorname{im}F_m\), and chooses the child removed by its unique predecessor. Stop the entire experiment at the first failed requirement. Let \(G\) be the event that the forward prefix and every local requirement succeed. Thus (2) uses one block exposure, not two independent exposures.

Let \(S\) be the sum of \(|\lambda_u|\) over all accepted new forward labels, the two accepted split labels when present, and all accepted continuation inverse labels before stopping. In particular \(|U|\le S\) on every outcome. The experiment uses at most \(s-s_0\) block exposures if \(r=0\), and at most \(s-s_0+2r-1\) if \(r\ge1\), always at most \(2Q\). All exposed blocks are distinct. Uniformly over the fixed data and both product laws,
$$
\mathbb E_{\mu_{a\lambda}}e^{cS}\le e^{1/1000}
\quad(0\le c\le24),\qquad
\mathbb P_{\mu_{a\lambda}}(G^c)<\frac1{1000}.
\tag{3}
$$
Consequently the original-mass and cubic good-event estimates are
$$
\mathbb E_{\mu_{\lambda}}\!\left[e^{2U}\mathbf1_{\mathcal P}\right]\le1.01,
\qquad
\mathbb E_{\mu_{3\lambda}}\!\left[e^{6U}\mathbf1_G\right]\ge0.99.
\tag{4}
$$

On \(G\) with \(r\ge1\), use exactly the \(2^{r-1}\) disjoint triples (4)-(5) of abbc24783c13e0f6 below \(j\), and add its singleton. Write \(R_j\) for this row and put \(c_0=1\), \(c_r=1+3\cdot2^{r-1}\) for \(r\ge1\), so \(|R_j|=c_r\). These are the same row sizes used in 1af079babe686d6e. Define the row score and its average square by
$$
Y_j(x)=\lambda\cdot(x-j),\qquad
V_j=\frac1{c_r}\sum_{x\in R_j}Y_j(x)^2.
\tag{5}
$$
For \(r=0\), (5) gives \(V_j=0\). Set the quantity \(V_j\mathbf1_G\) to zero on failure, without constructing a nontrivial row there. Then
$$
\mathbb E_{\mu_{3\lambda}}\!\left[e^{6U}V_j\mathbf1_G\right]\le1.01<2.
\tag{6}
$$
The same score is the full affine log score if the field outside \(\mathcal W\) is arbitrary but fixed, since these rows preserve every such coordinate; a common unchanged height also contributes zero to the score.

More explicitly, consider one fixed level \(s\), continuation length \(r\), and fixed-data class as above. Give its centers the actual affine weights
\(w_j=\mathfrak a\exp(\sum_{u\in\mathcal W}\lambda_u b_u+2U)\), where \(\mathfrak a>0\) is the factor from all fixed coordinates, fixed prefix spikes, and any common height. The weights on the row sources are those of this same affine law on the full support. Put \(P_a=\prod_{u\in\mathcal W}(1+e^{a\lambda_u})\). Source-to-level injectivity gives the following actual finite sums:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j:\mathcal P}w_j&\le1.01\,\mathfrak a P_1,\\
\sum_{j:G}c_r^2w_j^3&\ge0.99\,c_r^2\mathfrak a^3P_3,\\
\sum_{j:G}c_r^2w_j^3V_j&\le1.01\,c_r^2\mathfrak a^3P_3.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
$$
Here each sum includes every free Boolean assignment in the indicated event; no label or future success event is held fixed. Thus the squared-score average under these successful-row cubic weights is at most \(101/99<2\). The factor \(c_r^2\) cancels because \(r\) is fixed before the bits are sampled. In the mixed-row convention of 1af079babe686d6e, using singleton rows on test failure adds zero score numerator and nonnegative energy denominator, so the same bound holds after those centers are restored. It also persists when disjoint fixed-data and level classes are summed. In particular it applies with \(r=Q_t-s\) in any fixed level-height cell of that fact's complete lift. No conclusion here bounds the probability of encountering an additional strong block; that issue is excluded by the explicit weak-query hypothesis above.
